title: How Does Matter Change When Heated or Cooled?
icans: explain what happens to water when it is heated or cooled.

captions.text: Pensacola Beach, Florida. It looks like snow, but it's soft white sand.
Then, on January 21, 2025, real snow fell in Florida!
High in freezing clouds, water turned into snow. Fields turned white.
That night, the air stayed below freezing.
Sunlight warmed the snow, and it melted into water.
Soon even the puddles were gone. Where did the water go?
What happens to matter when it gets hotter or colder?

words: Matter with a fixed shape. Solids keep their shape unless a force changes them.
Matter that flows and takes the shape of its container. Water and juice are liquids.
Matter that spreads out to fill all the space available. Air is a gas.
When a solid gets warm enough to turn into a liquid. Ice melts into water.
When a liquid gets cold enough to turn into a solid. Water freezes into ice.
When a liquid turns into a gas. Warmth makes it happen faster. Puddles evaporate on sunny days.
When a gas cools and turns back into a liquid. Water drops on a cold glass are condensation.

parts.title: Three States of Matter
parts.html:
All matter is a solid, a liquid, or a gas. A rock is a solid. Juice is a liquid. The air around you is a gas.

Water is special. You can find it in all three states. Ice is solid water. Water vapor is water as a gas, and you can't see it.

parts.title: Heating Changes Matter
parts.html:
When you add heat, matter can change state. If ice gets warm enough, it melts into liquid water.

Liquid water can also evaporate. It turns into water vapor and mixes into the air. Warmth makes evaporation faster, so puddles dry quickly on hot days. Water doesn't have to boil to evaporate.

parts.title: Cooling Changes It Back
parts.html:
The Sun's light heats land, water, and air. At night or in the shade, the Sun's heat is missing, so things lose heat and cool down.

Cooling works the opposite way from heating. When water vapor cools, it turns back into tiny drops of liquid. That is condensation. When liquid water gets cold enough, it freezes into ice.

wall.rule: Heating and cooling change the state of water. The Sun's heat makes water evaporate. Cooling turns water vapor back into drops, and freezing cold turns water into ice.

wow.title: The Snowflake Man
wow.alt: A man in a hat and coat bends over a big old camera on a wooden stand outside a farmhouse
wow.caption: Wilson Bentley with his snowflake camera, Vermont
wow.html:
In 1885, a Vermont farmer named Wilson Bentley became the first person to photograph a single snowflake. He hooked a microscope to his camera and worked out in the cold, so the flakes would not melt.

He photographed more than 5,000 snowflakes. The mystery specimen at the start of this lesson is one of his photos!

keyIdea: Matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas. Adding heat can melt a solid into a liquid and evaporate a liquid into a gas. Taking heat away can condense a gas back into a liquid and freeze a liquid into a solid. The Sun heats water, land, and air; when the Sun is gone, they cool.

items.reveal: On freezing nights, farmers spray water on their fruit trees. The water freezes into a coat of ice that helps protect the buds. Florida orange growers use this trick too.

items.reveal: Kīlauea lava erupts at about 1,170 °C. When it cools in the air, it freezes into solid black rock. That's brand-new land! Later, ferns grow on it.
items.bts: Scientists use the word freezing for any liquid that turns solid, even melted rock.

items.reveal: In summer, the Sun warms Grinnell Glacier. Its ice melts into water that fills the lake below. The glacier is much smaller today than it was 100 years ago.

items.envAlt: A wide, grassy marsh under a blue sky with puffy clouds
items.envCap: Sawgrass prairie · Everglades National Park, Florida
items.reveal: In Florida's dry season, the Sun heats shallow ponds day after day. The water evaporates, and the mud dries and cracks. When the rains come back, the ponds fill again.
items.bts: From about November to April, the Everglades get much less rain. Scientists call it the dry season.

items.alt: A spider web covered in tiny, shiny drops of water

clues.t: Tiny drops of water on a spider web in the morning

clues.miss: Look again. Are the drops liquid or solid?

items.envMiss: The night air cooled the web. Was heat added or taken away? Try again.
items.envAlt: Drops of morning dew on a green blade of grass
items.reveal: On a cool night, water vapor in the air touches cold things and condenses into drops of dew. When the Sun rises, the dew evaporates again.
items.bts: Dew is not rain. It forms right on the spot, from water vapor in the air.

quiz.q: What happens to ice when it is heated?

options.t: It melts and becomes liquid water
options.ok: 🌲 Correct! When ice is heated, it melts. It changes from a solid to a liquid.

options.miss: Think about what happens to an ice cube left on a warm plate. Does it stay solid?

options.t: It turns directly into a gas
options.miss: Think about what happens to an ice cube left on a warm plate. Does it stay solid?

options.t: When a gas turns into a liquid
options.miss: Evaporation is about a liquid changing. Think about what happens to puddles on a hot sidewalk.

options.t: When a liquid heats up and turns into a gas
options.ok: 🌲 Yes! Evaporation is when a liquid turns into a gas, like puddles drying on a sunny day.

options.t: When a solid breaks into smaller pieces
options.miss: Evaporation is about a liquid changing. Think about what happens to puddles on a hot sidewalk.

quiz.q: A student leaves a glass of water in the freezer overnight. In the morning, the water is ice. What change happened?

options.miss: The water was liquid, and now it is solid ice. What is the name for a liquid turning into a solid?
The water was liquid, and now it is solid ice. What is the name for a liquid turning into a solid?

options.ok: 🌲 Exactly! The liquid water froze. It changed from a liquid to a solid because it was cooled.

partA.title: Label the state changes
partA.do: Read each one. Pick the best answer, or type your answer.

items.q: Solid → Liquid: what is this change called?

options.ok: Yes. A solid that warms up melts into a liquid.

options.miss: Freezing goes the other way, liquid to solid. Which change turns a solid into a liquid?
Condensation turns a gas into a liquid. Here a solid becomes a liquid.

items.q: Liquid → Gas: what is this change called?

options.miss: Melting turns a solid into a liquid. Here a liquid becomes a gas.

options.ok: Yes. A liquid that evaporates turns into a gas.

options.miss: Freezing turns a liquid into a solid. Here a liquid becomes a gas.

items.q: Gas → Liquid: what is this change called?

options.miss: Evaporation goes the other way, liquid to gas. Which change turns a gas back into a liquid?
Freezing turns a liquid into a solid. Here a gas becomes a liquid.

options.ok: Yes. When water vapor cools, it condenses into liquid drops.
